title: You’ve read it before. Maybe quickly. Maybe without feeling it.
paragraphs: You’ve read it before. Maybe quickly. Maybe without feeling it.
That means time passed. That means decay settled in. That means whatever life was there… is long gone.
And if you’re honest, you didn’t just read Book of Ezekiel 37.
Because you’ve walked through that valley.
The hand of the Lord carried Ezekiel into that place, and God didn’t rush him through it. He made him walk back and forth among the bones.
“Behold, they were very many in the open valley; and indeed they were very dry.” (Ezekiel 37:2)
No pulse. No warmth. No hidden spark.
And then God asks something that feels almost cruel:
“Son of man, can these bones live?”
That question lands on you too.
Can this life you’re living… live again?
Can that prayer life come back?
Can that hunger for God return?
Can a heart that’s been numb for years feel again?
But you didn’t say it out loud.
Here’s what most people don’t realize…
This wasn’t just a prophecy about Israel coming back from exile.
But it was also a mirror.
Because God wasn’t just showing Ezekiel a future nation.
He was exposing a present condition.
“They say, ‘Our bones are dry, our hope is lost, and we ourselves are cut off.’” (Ezekiel 37:11)
That’s the quiet sentence you’ve been living inside.
Still look alive on the outside.
God doesn’t tell Ezekiel to organize the bones.
He says something that doesn’t make sense in a dead place:
“Prophesy to these bones… and say to them, ‘O dry bones, hear the word of the Lord!’” (Ezekiel 37:4)
Because life doesn’t come from the bones.
You’ve been trying to revive yourself with effort, discipline, and guilt.
But resurrection doesn’t come from effort.
And when the Word goes out… something happens.
You can have structure without life.
That’s where many are stuck right now.
“Prophesy to the breath… Come from the four winds, O breath, and breathe on these slain, that they may live.” (Ezekiel 37:9)
Now we’re not talking about structure.
This is where Holy Spirit enters the scene.
And that only comes when God breathes life into what was dead.
“And the breath came into them, and they lived, and stood upon their feet, an exceedingly great army.” (Ezekiel 37:10)
You’ve been waiting to feel alive before you respond to God.
But God is calling you to respond… while you still feel like bones.
This is where everything comes to a point.
Because this vision doesn’t stand alone.
Because the ultimate valley of dry bones wasn’t Ezekiel’s vision.
“For all have sinned and fall short of the glory of God.” (Romans 3:23)
And then comes the turning point:
“But God demonstrates His own love toward us, in that while we were still sinners, Christ died for us.” (Romans 5:8)
Jesus Christ stepped into the valley.
And resurrection wasn’t just for Him.
So is the valley of dry bones prophecy?
But it’s also your spiritual condition… without Christ.
“I will put My Spirit in you, and you shall live.” (Ezekiel 37:14)
Because silence is where dryness survives.
And if you know someone who looks alive but is slowly dying inside, don’t keep this to yourself. Send it to them. You’re not exposing them—you’re reaching for them.
